newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas gains on cold weather forecast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas gains on cold weather forecast.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices regained an average of 10 cents Wednesday in response to the expected colder weather in many parts of the U.S., industry sources said.

Gulf Coast prices firmed by about 10 cents to the $2.70 per million British thermal units area as temperatures in the Northeast were expected to dip to freezing levels by Saturday and talk of storage withdrawals surfaced.
At the Henry Hub, La., traders reported closing deals in the low-$2.70s early and the high-$2.60s late.
In the Midcontinent, prices jumped ahead of index levels into the high-$2.50s on most of the pipes.
Forecasters are calling for temperatures as much as 10 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal on Thursday and Friday in most of the Midwest, followed by more moderate weather.
The impending cold weather spurred more bying at the Chicago city-gate, where traders reported closing deals in the high-$2.80s to low-$2.90s, up about 10 cents from Tuesday.
In west Texas, the expected arrival of cooler temperatures pushed Permian prices about five cents higher into the mid-$2.50s.
At the southern California border, prices were similarly higher in the low-to-mid $2.70s as supplies remained tight in the northwestern U.S.
Bonneville Power Administration reported earlier Wednesday it was again offering no surplus power for Thursday delivery for the sixth consecutive day.
On the opposite coast, New York city-gate prices were up at least five cents to the mid-$2.90s in anticipation of colder weather this weekend.
Separately, Niagara Mohawk Power Corp reported earlier Wednesday its 610 megawatt Nine Mile Point nuclear power unit in Scriba, N.Y., tripped off line late Tuesday due to a generator problem.
The company said it expects to resume power production by this weekend.
